SPECIFICATION FOR PAUSHTl K BARLEY POWDER
0. 0.1 FOREWORD

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 May 1984, after the draft finalized by the Nutrition Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Barley powder is a comparatively much finer material than whole Barley powder is manufactured by gradual reduction meal barley flour. of barley grains, pearl barley or barley grits by a roller milling process similar to that employed in milling wheat to maida.

0.3 In an effort at, nutritional upgrading, paushtik barley powder to which edible oilseed protein flour, vitamins and minerals have been added is at present being prepared and marketed in the country. This standard is expected to help in exercising proper quality control in the manufacture of paushtik barley powder of good quality under hygienic conditions. 0.4 ( IS afia out An Indian Standard has been brought out on barley powder s e p arate standards on fortified and paushtik wheat : 1157-1'J57* ). and wheat maidu and fortified barley powder are also being brought simultaneously.

NOTE - The paushtik variety contains higher percentage to the fortified variety, the percentage of other contents, and vitamins remaining the same.

0.5 While ftirmulating this standard, due consideration has been given to the relevant Rules prescribed by the Government of India, under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Standards of Weights and This standard is, however, Measures ( Packaged Commodities ) Rubs, 1977. subject to the restrictions imposed under these wherever applicabIe. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in The number of significant places accordance with IS : 2-19601_. retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
ing

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampland test for paushtik barley powder, hereafter termed PB powder.

2. REQUIREMENTS

2.1 The PB powder shall be prepared by uniformly blending, sufficient proportioris of an edible protein source ( up to 10 percent, also see Note 1 ), such as edible oilseed proteins, calcium carbonate, iron, thiamine, riboflavin and niacin with a barley powder of good quality ( see IS : 1157-1957* ). Skim milk powder ( see IS : 1165-1975t ) may also It shall be in the form of powder be blended in suitable proportions. having a characteristic taste and flavour. The product shall be free from rancidity and from insect, rodent or fungus infestation. It shall also musty or other objectionable odour. It shall be free from fermented, not have any ingredients other than those specified nor any extraneous matter.
NOTE 1 - In the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, only the addition of groundnut flour is permitted in similar products. Till such time as the addition of other protein rich flours is accepted by the Government of India, the granting of ISI Certification Mark shall he based on the existing requirements given under the Provisions of the Preuention of Food Adulferation Rules, 1955 ( see 0.5 ). NOTE 2 -The evaluation tests. 2.2 appearance, taste and odour shall be determined by sensory

2.2.2 UrEase Activity - The PB powder shall not show a change in PH by more than O-5, when determined by the method given in Appendix D of IS : 7837-1975t. 2.2.3 Gos.ykol - The PB powder shall not have a free gossypol content of more than 0.06 percent by mass and a total gossypol content of more than 1.2 percent by mass, when tested by the method given in Appendices A and B respectively of IS : 109Gl-1984:. 2.3 The calcium carbonate used for blending PB powder shall be as crpta preparata ) or dicalcium prepared chalk ( popularly known The iron or iron salts should be phosphate or tricalcium phosphate.
